precise_q1_lemma.statement: For every fixed real C>=1 and nonnegative integers R,S, there exist constants A0>0 and x0>=2, depending only on C,R,S, such that for every real x>=x0, every integer a with |a|<=C*x^2, and every interval J contained in [1,C*x], sum over integers b in J, b!=a of tau(b)^R*tau(|b-a|)^S <= A0*x*(1+log x)^E, where E=(2^(2R)+2^(2S)-2)/2. Enlarging A0 handles 2<=x<x0. No lower bound on |a| is required.
derivation: For each nonnegative integer e, f(n)=tau(n)^e is nonnegative multiplicative and satisfies Shiu's growth hypotheses: f(p^l)=(l+1)^e<=2^(el), and tau(n)^e=O_e,epsilon(n^epsilon).

Use primitive Shiu at modulus 1, with its independent parameters alpha_Sh=1/4 and kappa_Sh=1/8. An image interval of |b-a| has length <=Cx and location <=C*x^2+Cx. It splits into at most two positive intervals with multiplicity at most two.
For a positive image interval beginning below 2Cx, all its values are <=3Cx and the ordinary mean of tau(n)^e is O_C,e(x*(1+log x)^(2^e-1)); e=0 is the counting case.

For an image interval beginning at X>=2Cx, enlarge to [X,X+2Cx). Then Y=2Cx<=X and X^(1/8)<=Y for all sufficiently large x uniformly over X<=C*x^2+Cx. Modulus 1<Y^(3/4), so Shiu applies. Since f(p)=2^e and the prime reciprocal sum is loglog X+O(1), its bound is O_C,e(Y*(log X)^(2^e-1))=O_C,e(x*(1+log x)^(2^e-1)).

Use e=2S on the nonzero shifted values and e=2R on unshifted b. Cauchy gives the displayed exponent E. Integer endpoints can be absorbed by the chosen 2Cx enlargement or ordinary mean bound; no tau(0) term is introduced.

The original |a|<=x^(1+kappa) is inside this lemma's |a|<=C*x^2 uniformly for all original kappa. Thus this branch covers every allowed fixed B and kappa; there is no tradeoff between moment order and residue exponent.

classical_source.fixed_version: Thomas Wright, A Shiu Theorem for Larger and Smoother Functions, arXiv:2508.17217v1, 24 August 2025, Theorem 1.1 (classical Shiu 1980 restatement)
classical_source.verification: Fresh primary authored-paper HTML read, theorem at lines 58-79; also local saved text bound below. We use only its classical Theorem 1.1, not the different new results.
classical_source.input: For fixed admissible multiplicative f and alpha_Sh,kappa_Sh in (0,1/2), when X^kappa_Sh<=Y<=X, q<Y^(1-alpha_Sh), and gcd(r,q)=1, Shiu bounds the progression sum by Y/[phi(q) log X] times exp(sum_{p<=X,p not dividing q}f(p)/p). Here q=1.
classical_source.formal_status: Classical analytic input, not a checked Lean artifact. No claim of zero-sorry source, full Lean type or axiom certificate.

elementary_alternative.exact_statement: For fixed integers R,S>=0 and fixed C>=1, put K=2^(2*max(R,S,1)). The source proves uniformly for x>=2, |a|<=C*x^(1+kappa), J subset [1,Cx], 0<=kappa<=1/(2K), the same mixed sum <=O_C,R,S(x*(1+log x)^(K-1)).
elementary_alternative.why_cap_appears: The source's elementary short-interval d_K estimate has remainder x^((1+kappa)*(1-1/K)). Its stated cap makes this exponent <=1-1/(2K)-1/(2K^2)<1. This is a sufficient condition for this proof; failure of it is not a counterexample to the actual mixed-moment bound.
elementary_alternative.cannot_select_K_for_arbitrary_given_kapp: K must dominate the required squared divisor orders. For fixed kappa>0, the stated cap requires K<=1/(2kappa), while the source construction requires K>=2^(2*max(R,S,1)). Those need not be compatible. Increasing K worsens the cap. No assertion is made that a different elementary proof could not do better.
elementary_alternative.logical_nonimplication_example: Allowed sigma=1/1000 and kappa=sigma/100=1/100000, with B=20 in beta truncation, give R=B+2=22 and S=3, so the displayed elementary K=2^44 requires kappa<=2^(-45), which fails. This is a counterexample only to automatic implication of the extra gate, not to the manuscript theorem or to any moment estimate.
elementary_alternative.actual_application_parameter_order: After geometry/reserves, zeta/sigma, rough precision, finite rank J and all actual moment orders are fixed, take finite K_mom=max_i 2^(2*max(R_i,S_i,1)), including S=2J after the outer boundary Cauchy (hence tau^(4J)). Choose positive rational kappa<=min(sigma/200,1/(2K_mom)), then positive kappa0<kappa/[4(1+kappa)] and all existing support caps. Positive choices exist because K_mom is finite and sigma>0. This is an existential application choice, not a change to the fixed-kappa theorem.
elementary_alternative.retained_scale_check: If c*T^(1-kappa0)<=x<=C*T, then x^(1+kappa)>=c^(1+kappa)*T^((1-kappa0)*(1+kappa)). Its exponent is 1+kappa-kappa0*(1+kappa)>1+3kappa/4>1; hence T<=x^(1+kappa) eventually. x<=C*T gives c0*x<=T for any c0<=1/C. The discarded T^(1-kappa0+o(1)) remains o(T/log(T)^A) for each fixed A. Moment orders precede log precision and T, preventing a circular dependence.
